Presence-specific data binding must stay in Knit; only the generic presentation layer moves to Looma. Per the migration inventory this is a B-category promotion candidate.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Generic ui-avatar-group component ships in @looma/core with domain-neutral API (no workspace/presence vocabulary)
React and Vue adapter exports exist for AvatarGroup
Contract README, Docusaurus page, and Storybook story all ship in the same change
pnpm generate:api && pnpm check:docs-sync pass
Knit's AvatarGroup.vue is updated to consume the new Looma primitive

tasks.description: The comments table already exists in the Supabase schema. This task implements the API endpoints and UI for inline/page comments: select text → add comment, thread replies, show comments on page. This is item #5 in the Knit feature roadmap parity list.

Comments appear in a sidebar or inline indicator on the page
Thread replies work (add reply, display thread)

subdomain utils has tests covering: extractWorkspaceSlug and workspaceHost for valid, invalid, and edge-case inputs

tasks.title: Generate TypeScript types from Supabase schema
tasks.description: Run pnpm db:types to generate proper TypeScript types from the Supabase schema and wire them into the codebase. Currently Knit uses ad-hoc types. This is a V1 polish item and will improve type safety across all server API routes and composables.
outOfScope: Migrating all files to use generated types in one pass (incremental adoption is fine)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Generated types file exists at the expected output path after running pnpm db:types
At least the server/api and composables directories import from generated types where the types overlap with existing ad-hoc types
pnpm typecheck passes after adoption

tasks.title: Ground worker mutations in real repo surfaces before code edits
tasks.description: Before a worker writes or edits code, Guildhall should force the task through a repo-grounding pass that proves the imported files, component paths, and local UI/API patterns actually exist. Guessed imports like a nonexistent LoomaButton.vue should be blocked or rewritten from grounded repo evidence before the task can claim completion.
outOfScope: Broad semantic linting of every possible implementation choice

acceptanceCriteria.description: When a worker proposes a new local import or component path, Guildhall either has durable evidence that the path exists or blocks the move with a grounded recovery prompt before review handoff
Live Looma or Knit task replays stop inventing nonexistent local components when an equivalent grounded repo pattern already exists

tasks.title: Persist richer durable resume context for long-running worker tasks
tasks.description: Recovery checkpoints should capture enough task-local context that a restarted worker resumes with the same narrowed picture it had before: authoritative verification command results, companion files, current working hypothesis, and the safe next mutation surface.
outOfScope: Full transcript replay as the default recovery mechanism

acceptanceCriteria.description: Recovery checkpoints persist authoritative verification outcomes plus narrowed task-local context beyond touched files and next action
After restart, resumed workers receive that durable context and continue from the narrowed mutation surface instead of broad rediscovery

tasks.title: Prove unattended throughput in staged queue runs
tasks.description: After provider/runtime and lane scheduling are trustworthy, prove Guildhall can continue through a queue in stages: one real task merged, three tasks processed without manual restart, then a longer run that stops only when blocked or exhausted.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Guildhall can process at least three real unblocked tasks in one unattended run with explicit blocked accounting
Longer queue runs stop with a truthful exhausted-or-blocked summary instead of silent stalls

tasks.title: Move Looma to public GitHub and prepare MIT/package publishing
tasks.description: Prepare Looma to be a public, reusable foundation for Guildhall-generated and user projects. Move or mirror the current Looma repository from its legacy Bitbucket Granola remote to github.com/threadlabs-studio/looma, set up proper MIT licensing, and verify the package publishing plan for the existing @threadlabs npm org. This task is tracking/setup work first: audit current local changes, remote state, package scopes, license headers, docs, CI, and release implications before pushing or publishing.
outOfScope: Changing Looma component APIs except where required for package metadata or licensing
Publishing npm packages before the repository/license/package plan is reviewed
Force-pushing or rewriting any shared remote history without explicit approval
Making Guildhall depend on a local Looma checkout for normal users

acceptanceCriteria.description: Current Looma repo state is audited: active branch, dirty files, existing Bitbucket remote, package names/scopes, license files, CI/release scripts, and Storybook/docs publish surfaces are documented in a task note or artifact
GitHub remote strategy is implemented or ready for approval for git@github.com:threadlabs-studio/looma.git without losing existing history
MIT license is added or verified at the repo root, and package/docs metadata clearly identify Looma as MIT-licensed
Package publishing plan for the @threadlabs npm org is documented, including package names, access level, versioning, and any migration from @looma/* names
CI/release readiness is verified with Looma checks such as pnpm install, pnpm typecheck, pnpm build, pnpm test, and docs/Storybook build where available
acceptanceCriteria.command: pnpm install && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm build:docs && pnpm build:storybook

acceptanceCriteria.description: Guildhall 0.9 design-quality tracker is updated with the final Looma public/MIT/package status and any follow-up tasks
